List All Files in a Directory Recursively with Full Paths [python]

The Code

from pathlib import Path

def list_files(dir):
    result = []
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in Path(dir).resolve().walk():
        dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if not d.startswith('.')]
        for name in filenames:
            if not (name.startswith('.') or name.endswith('~')):
                result.append(dirpath / name)
    return sorted(result)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    with open("output.inc.txt", "w") as _out:
        for f in list_files("examples.inc"):
            _out.write(f"{str(f)}\n")

Notes

  • This uses Path's .walk instead of os.walk so that Path objects are returned instead of strings. This requires python 3.12 or later.

  • Full paths are returned.

  • You can get relative paths by removing the .resolve() method from the Path(dir) call.

  • This skips hidden direcotires that start with a dot and temporary files that end with a ~.

  • The dirnames[:] = [d for d in dirnames if not d.startswith('.')] line updates the directory name in place so that os.walk skips the hidden directories entirely instead of decending into them.

  • The results are sorted before returning them from the method.
